scenario.name: Kaspersky GReAT, Citizen Lab & Amnesty MVT — iOS Operation Triangulation Zero-Click iMessage & Shutdown.log Forensics (CVE-2023-41990)
scenario.overview: Imagine a ghost burglar slipping into a locked smartphone apartment through an unread postcard slid under the front door without the homeowner ever tapping the screen. The burglar works strictly in the dark, burns every paper note in the hallway before leaving, and vanishes whenever the building power cycles; yet the elevator’s nightly closing log still records an unfamiliar worker lingering in the storage corridor and the utility meter permanently shows megabytes of unexplained water flowing out of an unused closet. In this scenario (T1456, Kaspersky GReAT, Citizen Lab & Amnesty MVT, iOS Operation Triangulation Zero-Click iMessage & Shutdown.log Forensics , CVE-2023-41990), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: hidden iMessage Attachment Processing, then ephemeral Implant Execution, then anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing, then Ephemeral Implant Execution, then Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1456 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1456 - Drive-By Compromise / Zero-Click Messaging)
stages.description: Before the homeowner even wakes the phone screen, the building’s automated mail sorter opens the rigged postcard in the basement mailroom, triggering an invisible print-shop jam that leaves behind a faint diagnostic receipt on the maintenance clipboard. When a zero-click iMessage containing a crafted font/image attachment arrives via Apple Push Notification service (apsd), imagent and IMTranscoderAgent process the attachment automatically. Forensic artifacts in CrashReporter and diagnostic logs record abnormal memory faults inside FontParser / CoreGraphics (logged in Linux Audit Event 41990 with TargetDaemon=IMTranscoderAgent , iMessage Attachment Transcoder, LibraryModule=libFontParser.dylib , TrueType ADJUST Instruction, VulnerabilityRef=CVE-2023-41990 / CVE-2023-32434 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mvt-ios check-backup --output ./mvt-results ./ios-encrypted-backup/ (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1456 during "Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace"). Next, the follow-up artifact mvt-ios check-iocs --iocs triangulation.stix2 ./mvt-results/ runs (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1456 during "Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace"). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/IMTranscoderAgent.framework/IMTranscoderAgent / ⇠#1 ACK 41990) from Node ① (#1 Zero-Click iMessage Attachment) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shutdown.log & DataUsage.sqlite).

stages.title: Stage 2: Ephemeral Implant Execution in /private/var/tmp/ Recorded in iOS Shutdown.log
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.004 - Indicator Removal: File Deletion / Shutdown.log)
stages.description: The ghost burglar runs quietly out of a temporary hallway locker and shreds their working files immediately afterward, forgetting that every time the building powers down, the master elevator log writes down the exact badge number and locker path of every worker still lingering at closing time. Even though the in-memory implant removes its temporary files from /private/var/tmp/ after execution and does not survive a reboot, the iOS kernel writes every unclosed process PID and path active during system shutdown into /private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log (extracted from a sysdiagnose archive) (logged in Linux Audit Event 38606 with ForensicArtifactFile=/private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log , sysdiagnose, RecordedProcessPath=/private/var/tmp/main, ForensicSignificance=Proves execution of deleted binary from world-writable /private/var/tmp/ so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "/private/var/tmp/|/private/var/db/" sysdiagnose_extracted/logs/Shutdown/shutdown.log (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , grep -E "/pr so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1070.004 during "Ephemeral Implant Execution in /private/var/tmp/ Recorded in iOS Shutdown.log"). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ /private/var/tmp/main (Recorded in /private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log) / ⇠#2 ACK 38606) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 IMTranscoderAgent / BlastDoor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shutdown.log & DataUsage.sqlite).

keySpecs.value: Collect a full iOS sysdiagnose archive prior to wiping a suspected device and run mvt-ios over Shutdown.log to identify processes that executed from /private/var/tmp/.

stages.title: Stage 3: Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi Exfiltration in DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration Over C2 Channel)
stages.description: Even days after a reboot wipes the ghost burglar out of memory, the building’s permanent water-and-power billing books still display heavy outbound usage billed to a broom-closet service that should never transmit anything to the street. iOS persistently tracks per-process network byte counters in /private/var/wireless/Library/Databases/DataUsage.sqlite and netusage.sqlite. MVT correlates ZPROCESS entries showing non-networked system daemons (or deleted PIDs) transmitting megabytes of HTTPS data over Wi-Fi/Cellular (logged in Network Event 443 with SqliteDatabase=DataUsage.sqlite / netusage.sqlite, AnomalousProcessName=BackupAgent , ZPROCNAME with NULL Bundle ID, OutboundBytesRecorded=14.8 MB Wi-Fi / 3.1 MB Cellular so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIIN, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIOUT FROM ZLIVEUSAGE JOIN ZPROCESS ON ZLIVEUSAGE.ZHASPROCESS = ZPROCESS.Z_PK;" (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLI so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1041 during "Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi Exfiltration in DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite SELECT ZPROCNAME, ZWIFIOUT FROM ZLIVEUSAGE / ⇠#3 RESP 443) from Node ③ (#3 IMTranscoderAgent / BlastDoor) to Node ④ (#4 XNU Kernel & MMIO Registers), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shutdown.log & DataUsage.sqlite).

keySpecs.value: sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIIN, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIOUT FROM ZLIVEUSAGE JOIN ZPROCESS ON ZLIVEUSAGE.ZHASPROCESS = ZPROCESS.Z_PK;"
